clues: This port city sits in north Germany where a small river joins a wide river mouth. Big ships reach the North Sea from its docks.
Snow falls here in winter, but it soon melts and does not stay on the ground. Hard frost and heat waves are rare in this mild sea air.
It was founded in 1827 as a new sea port for a nearby trading city. Ships have used its docks ever since that bold start.
Odd but true, this port is a scrap of one city state set far from the rest of it. Other land wraps all the way round it.
This port spent eight years as part of a bigger city, Wesermünde. It was made in 1924 when the port's rival town joined with the town next door, and this port was handed back in 1947.
